title.narrative: In 2025, adolescent girls' programming anchored in what works for girls and gender-responsive parenting and gender integration in immunization emerged as key strategic priorities. Through strengthened partnerships with Plan International and Oxfam, efforts focused on empowering adolescent girls, centring their voices, and generating practical evidence on effective, gender programming for transformational results approaches in the MENA region.This collaboration resulted in the AGILE report, which captures evidence on what works best for adolescent girls in MENA, informed by field visits and participatory research led by girls engaged in UNICEF-supported programmes and the She Leads initiative under Plan International. In parallel, a girl-led, gender-responsive NDC review guidance was developed and showcased at the Youth Climate Change Summit in Salalah, Oman, demonstrating the integration of adolescent girls' leadership into climate and policy spaces.In addition, a regional training on gender-responsive parenting was delivered in February 2025 to UNICEF MENA Country Offices and their implementing partners, strengthening technical capacity on GRP approaches. This was complemented by a mapping exercise of GRP programmes across MENA, aimed at developing practical, regionally adaptable materials and building the capacity of frontline workers and parents of children aged 0 18 years.The MENA Regional Office developed a coherent body of gender-, equity-, and community health focused evidence, case studies, and learning products to address persistent barriers to immunization and strengthen primary health care and community health systems, particularly in fragile and conflict-affected settings. To strengthen linkages between evidence and programming, a regional consultant was engaged to work closely with MENA Country Offices, resulting in:Gender analyses on barriers to immunizationCase studies and country insights: from evidence to actionUNICEF Gender Analytical Review Six-Part Learning Series (2025In addition, diverse and targeted technical support was provided to Country Offices throughout 2025 to strengthen gender integration and programme quality. This included support on Gender Programmatic Reviews (GPRs) for Jordan and Sudan, the development of a regional gender roster, and an evaluability assessment for Syria. Technical missions and collaboration also supported Iraq, including contributions to a brief for BMZ outlining progress to date and proposed strategic next steps under Power4Girls, aimed at strengthening evidence-based advocacy and resource mobilization.
